The trial was terminated early due to lack of patient recruitment (only 30 patients enrolled, trial terminated for lack of patients), meaning the primary endpoint was never reached and no efficacy readout was obtained. There is no evidence of target engagement for either iron supplement or Vitamin E on oxidative stress pathways. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarker data available. Calprotectin measurements were planned at baseline, week 4, week 6, and week 10, but outcomes are listed as unknown, consistent with early termination before data collection was complete. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint (calprotectin in stools) was not met — no results were reported. This is an operational failure due to recruitment collapse rather than a mechanistic failure. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses were conducted or reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial was explicitly terminated due to lack of patients (investigator commentary: 'Trial terminated due to lack of patients'). With only 30 patients enrolled and no efficacy readout, this is a classic operational failure — the causal chain was never given a fair test. The mechanism was not tested, and no conclusions about the biology can be drawn.
